headline: Experts warn dengue cases could double in July
summary: Health experts are raising alarms as the risk of a surge in dengue fever infections increases throughout the month.
details: Health experts have warned that the number of dengue cases in Bangladesh may double by the end of July.
The warning comes as the monsoon season progresses, creating ideal conditions for the breeding of Aedes mosquitoes.
Authorities are urging the public to maintain strict hygiene and eliminate stagnant water around their homes to prevent outbreaks.
Medical professionals are emphasizing the importance of early detection and diagnosis to reduce the risk of complications and fatalities.
caption:
Dengue cases could double this month. Experts are warning of a potential surge.

Health experts have warned that the number of dengue cases in Bangladesh may double by the end of July.

The warning comes as the monsoon season progresses, creating ideal conditions for the breeding of Aedes mosquitoes.

Authorities are urging the public to maintain strict hygiene and eliminate stagnant water around their homes to prevent outbreaks.

Medical professionals are emphasizing the importance of early detection and diagnosis to reduce the risk of complications and fatalities.

Source: Dhaka Tribune

headline_marked: Inspiring: [[Student writes HSC exam using her foot]] in Rangpur
headline: Inspiring: Student writes HSC exam using her foot in Rangpur
summary: Born without wrists, Koli Rani's determination to pursue higher education is defying physical limitations to achieve her dream of becoming a BCS cadre.
details: Koli Rani, a student from Gadai village in Rangpur's Kaunia upazila, is taking her Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) exams using her right foot. Born without wrists, she has overcome significant physical limitations to pursue her education.

Koli Rani is appearing for the humanities group at the Kaunia Mahila College center. To support her, she has been granted an additional 30 minutes of writing time per exam, as per official regulations for students with disabilities.

Her journey has not been easy, as she faced poverty and physical challenges from a childhood. Despite this, she earned an 'A' grade in Class 5 and successfully passed her SSC exams by writing with her foot.

Beyond academics, Koli Rani is a talented singer and has received multiple awards and honors. She is also proficient in using computers and mobile phones using her feet, demonstrating her versatility and skills.

Koli Rani's ultimate goal is to become a BCS cadre to serve the people of Bangladesh. The local administration, including the Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Papia Sultana, has pledged their full support to ensure she reaches her higher education goals.

Her brother, Montu Ram Rai, shared that while her hands were too small and curved to hold a pen, her extraordinary willpower has driven her success. Her story is now serving as an inspiration to many across the country.
